incident-bot: [ALERT] IncidentID: INC-20260310-aurora-padlock
Severity: Sev2 - SLO breach
Metric: streaming.p99_latency = 2800ms (SLO 2000ms), p95 = 420ms (SLO 200ms)
Concurrent_sessions: 320 (baseline ~80) | qps ~140
Observed: streaming stalls / long tail token latency >10s for a subset (~0.6% requests).
Affected: single-tenant = aurora-padlock (tenant_id: cust-aurora-padlock)
Paging: @sara oncall
Link: https://monitoring.internal/redwood/incidents/INC-20260310-aurora-padlock

sara: Acked. I'm on it. Bringing dev oncall. @devon @maya — what's current impact? Are we seeing errors or just latency?

devon: pulling graphs now, quick numbers from Datadog: p50 80ms, p95 420ms, p99 2800ms, p999 tail spikes ~12s.
qps ~140 (normally ~60) — looks like a burst of concurrent sessions. error-rate not elevated (~0.3%) — mainly slow streaming tokens.
Also seeing a huge spike in kvcache.evictions/sec (700x).

maya: likely KV-cache thrash + huge prefixes. Customer's recent prompt pattern includes lots of repeated system tokens and very long context (~28k tokens) causing streaming stalls at the tail. Immediate mitigation options:
1) route affected tenant to fallback smaller model to reduce KV pressure
2) enable aggressive prefix/KV caching (prefix_only) for the tenant
3) apply per-tenant concurrency throttle (limit new sessions)
4) fallback to non-streaming mode for affected sessions (less tail sensitivity)
Which should we try first?

ingrid: I'll apply routing override to fallback-model-v2 now for cust-aurora-padlock. Patching router: 
```
curl -X POST https://routing.internal/api/v1/route-override \
  -d '{"tenant":"cust-aurora-padlock","model":"fallback-model-v2","ttl":600}' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ROUTER_TOKEN'
```
Reporting back when done.

ops-bot: Routing override applied for cust-aurora-padlock -> fallback-model-v2 (12 active sessions). Took 4.2s. re-route telemetry: success=12 fail=0

devon: after routing change p95 down to ~210ms, p99 ~750ms (big improvement). Some streaming sessions still show sporadic stalls at the tail (~2% of previously routed sessions). Still seeing kvcache.evictions high on nodes: gpu-node-14, gpu-node-15.
logs snippet:
```
[2026-03-10T14:02:12Z] session=abc123 token_idx=274 kvcache.eviction=true latency=11450ms
[2026-03-10T14:02:14Z] session=def456 token_idx=302 kvcache.hit=false latency=9800ms
```

sara: good improvement. Can we enable prefix-only KV caching and restart inference workers on the affected nodes? @kyle can you assist with node-level restarts / kernel-selection fallback?

kyle: I'll take node restarts and kernel fallback. I'll toggle `kv_cache.mode=prefix_only` for the tenant and drain/restart workers on gpu-node-14/15. Commands I'm going to run: 
```
rbctl set-tenant-config cust-aurora-padlock --kv_cache_mode=prefix_only
rbctl drain-node gpu-node-14 && rbctl restart-worker --node gpu-node-14
rbctl drain-node gpu-node-15 && rbctl restart-worker --node gpu-node-15
```
ETA ~6-8 minutes.

maya: also applying a temporary per-tenant concurrency cap of 40 to prevent new session spikes. Applying policy now: 
```
api apply-tenant-policy --tenant cust-aurora-padlock --max-concurrency 40 --reason 'mitigation'
```

ops-bot: Tenant policy applied. New sessions will be queued when concurrency >=40.

devon: after node restart + kv mode change p99 ~420ms, p95 ~160ms. Tail stalls are now rare (<0.1%). We should keep the fallback-model active for the next hour and run a deeper postmortem. Preliminary root cause hypothesis: combination of extremely long prompt context + repeated delimiter tokens causing KV cache churn under high concurrency.

sara: documenting customer impact: ~0.6% requests experienced >5s tail latency before mitigation; customer-facing errors minimal but streaming UX degraded for some sessions. Notifying CS to prepare a summary for Aurora. @ingrid can you capture the routing audit and exact timestamps?

ingrid: captured audit: routing override applied 2026-03-10T14:03:11Z, node restart initiated 2026-03-10T14:09:25Z (gpu-node-14) & 2026-03-10T14:12:08Z (gpu-node-15). Attaching logs to ticket INC-20260310-aurora-padlock.

kyle: handoff — I'm taking the mitigation window. I'll monitor heap/KV metrics for 30m and collect traces. If KV thrash resurfaces when we re-enable normal config, escalate to eng-runtime.

sara: handing off to kyle — I'm off at 1765433430. Thanks all. Next update +15m or sooner. :thumbsup:
